text:
The man is likely to prevail. When the woman conveyed the house to him, title to the dominant and servient parcels united in one owner and the recorded right-of-way ended by merger; his later warranty deed transferred only the house as he then held it and created no new right-of-way. The path was only a more direct route to the highway, and he never possessed or used the house, so the purchaser took no easement by necessity or by implication from a prior use.

CONFIDENCE: 88
